summary: Reconcile instant, admin-free team onboarding against an audit requirement that every access trace to an explicit grant, without breaking a frozen configuration contract.

contradictions.statement: Access derived from team membership at access time is what makes joining instant and admin-free, and it is exactly what Security forbids: a lookup leaves no record of what was visible, to whom, or when. Explicit grants normally arrive by an administrator step, which Product rules out.

max_grants_per_document is inert while access is derived and becomes load-bearing the moment grants are materialised — a team can carry more members than a document is configured to hold. The configuration contract forbids resolving this by renaming keys or adding required ones.

hard_constraints.statement: A file containing only default_visibility and max_grants_per_document loads and works.
Every allowed access traces to a grant record: if can_access is True, grants_for(document_id) holds an active record naming that user.
No implicit access: a directory reporting a user as a team member, with no grant present, must not confer access.
can_access(user_id, document_id, now), join_team(user_id, team_id, now) and leave_team(user_id, team_id, now) keep injected time; no clock reads.

interacting_constraints_note: HC2 and HC3 are the interacting pair, and HC2 alone is not enough: the seeded implementation violates both, while a scheme that renders grant records from current membership on demand satisfies HC2 and still violates HC3. Only HC3 separates a recorded decision from a rendered lookup. Neither document names that distinction.

evidence.fact_only_available_there: 2.1% of allowed accesses (88200 of 4200000) were by users who had already left the owning team but still resolved as members through a cache stale by up to six hours; team size reaches a p99 of 260 against a shipped max_grants_per_document of 250.
evidence.why_it_matters: The documents state that the directory is a cache and that the cap exists. Only the telemetry shows that the lag is real and load-bearing, that none of those accesses were recorded anywhere, and that a routine team is larger than the shipped cap. A document-only solution has no reason to treat revocation as an act with a timestamp, or to have handled a team that overruns the cap at all.

acceptance_suite.note: N15 §6.4 — must-pass designation is pinned with the manifest. success = all must-pass green AND zero hard-constraint violations.

distractors.reading: Access-time membership check, with grant records rendered from current membership on demand. Instant onboarding, and every allowed access appears to name a grant — but the records are a view of the lookup, so a stale row still confers access. Violates HC3.
Explicit grants only, provisioned by a separate administrator call. Auditable and stale-proof; joining a team grants nothing, which is the onboarding failure Product filed against.

deliverables.description: The change satisfying the reconciled requirements.
Decision record: what was decided, alternatives rejected, and exactly what happens when max_grants_per_document is reached.

calibration.solvability: sealed/reference passes the full suite; no LLM involved.
calibration.discrimination: PENDING — baseline saturation/floor check requires runs at both tiers (N15 §6.3(2)).
